title: Details of the Savoy bebop dates
summary: Hall recalls the personnel of the Savoy dates, sponsor Herman Lubinsky, and how the guys were selling tunes cheaply.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: When you did make these record dates, you know, the ones with Fats and Sonny Stitt, what do you remember about those dates in particular?

Well, they were different than any recordings that I had been making. The versatility of the performance. I was in awe, as far as versatility was concerned. The rhythm section just had to be a (inaudible) one. A Ray Brown or Oscar Pettiford. (Unaudible)
Well, I guess, did Kenny Clarke make those with you or Wally Bishop. Wally Bishop is on some of those and Kenny Clarke is on some of the others.
Kenny Clarke was on some of them and I think, yeah, basically Kenny.
Yeah, but --
Bud Powell.
Bud Powell.
And Sonny Stitt, Ray Abrams.
Oh, yeah, that was the other date.
These are all Savoy.
Yeah, with Eddie (inaudible), and Morris Lane on tenor.
Yes, yes, yes.
With Kenny (inaudible) and Fats Navarro.
Right. These were the first of that and.
Did you also make the date, there was one date for Savoy and one that Kenny made for French Swing the day before or the day after; you weren't on the Swing
No, no. These were all experimental things that Linsinsky sponsored.
Teddy Reig influenced them to do it.

Yeah, I guess so, but we were all out of work at the time and the guys were selling their compositions for a pittance, for 75 to pay the rent and so it was a matter of a record date rather than a gung-ho performance jazz-wise. It was just a matter of having a gig. That included me too.
But yet for someone like, you know, Sonny Stitt, it was his first big break on records.
Well, we didn't know it, we didn't understand it as such then. It only comes out later as creating some new phase, or whatever. But this was just new music that we exploited.
But as you said, the soloist had a
great degree of skill, technical skill.
Yeah, yeah.
